cells.tense: You are standing in the middle of what you helped make, and you can feel it.
cells.ask: Eat one meal you cooked for others at the table with them, not standing up.
cells.core:
You can tell what's finished and what still needs carrying. That's the working part of this — you don't need the whole thing perfect before you count it, and you don't hand over something you haven't actually lived. The people around you get the real version, and you feel the weight of what you've made without needing to defend it.

What feeds this next is showing up while it's still happening. Stay inside the thing you built instead of circling back to check it. Someone brings something of their own to the table — let that be part of what's already here rather than a problem to solve. The next good thing tends to grow from staying put. At the table, not standing over it.

cells.tense: You are bracing for the moment this finally lands the way it was supposed to.
cells.ask: Hand one piece of the work to someone else this week and leave their version alone.
cells.core:
You're pushing the good thing past where it already got to. There's a next version in your head that hasn't happened yet, and you keep steering toward it — so the thing in front of you doesn't get to be finished, and neither do you. Something in you wants it settled, and it reaches for that before the work has caught up.

What's underneath this wants room, not a plan. Let the thing you already made stand as it is and let someone else carry a piece. Care for it the way you'd water something growing, not the way you'd grip a handle. You'll know the difference — one leaves you with energy left.

cells.tense: You once said more of what you actually thought, and you have not said it since.
cells.ask: Bring one half-formed thing to one person this week that you have not shown anyone.
cells.core:
You have things worth passing on and you're sitting on them. The sharing went quiet somewhere, and now you'd rather keep the good thing private than say it and risk it landing flat. So what you know stays with you, and the people around you get less of what's already made.

Wanting to say it hasn't gone anywhere. It waits for you to trust your own read before you can prove it. Say one true thing to one person without working it out first. You don't need certainty to say it, and you're allowed to be a little unfinished in front of someone.

cells.tense: You are already shaping what gets passed down while telling yourself you are just watching.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you actually thought about a thing you both already know.
cells.core:
You're the one building what gets carried forward — in what you say is worth holding onto, in the version of the story that leaves the room with people. But it gets described like it's the material talking, or the tradition doing it by itself. The work is happening. Your name just isn't on it yet.

What's underneath is quiet and useful — you can tell what matters from what doesn't, and that's why your version holds. Say once that this is yours, without dressing it up. Pick the thing you've been feeling strongly about and name it as your call. It's already true. Someone should hear it from you.
